summary: Iteration 161 — Tested Custom Unsubscribe Flow. 12/12 backend pytest assertions PASS (verify/confirm endpoints, token util, suppression guard, URL injection, webhook handlers, full lifecycle). 4/4 frontend flows PASS via Playwright (EN garbage→error+support link, EN valid→masked email+Confirm button, click→success card 'You've been unsubscribed.', FR /desabonnement→'Se désabonner des courriels BidVex'+'Confirmer le désabonnement').

minor.issue: Does NOT upsert users doc (only $set on existing). If webhook fires for an email with no user record, marketing_unsubscribed is never recorded on users collection — only email_suppressions gets the entry. confirm() endpoint DOES upsert; consider aligning for consistency.

spamreport was moved from DELIVERABILITY_KILL_EVENTS to UNSUBSCRIBE_EVENTS as requested, BUT the admin spam alert (_send_spam_alert) is only called inside the DELIVERABILITY_KILL_EVENTS branch. Consequence: spam reports no longer trigger the '🚨 SPAM REPORT' admin email. If that alert is still wanted, also call _send_spam_alert from the UNSUBSCRIBE_EVENTS branch when etype=='spamreport'.

Collection name inconsistency: _handle_deliverability_kill writes to db.email_suppression (singular), while _handle_unsubscribe + confirm endpoint write to db.email_suppressions (plural). Admin endpoint /admin/email-suppression reads singular; send-time guard reads plural. Hard bounces therefore will NOT suppress marketing sends.

issues: Cookie Consent banner overlaps the 'Never mind, take me back' link and partially covers the Confirm button area on initial load — on a real user visit it could hide the CTA until dismissed. Consider temporarily collapsing the cookie banner on the /unsubscribe + /desabonnement routes, or raising the card above the banner.

action_items: Align suppression collection naming: use email_suppressions (plural) everywhere OR dual-write both. Current state: bounces land in singular, unsubscribes in plural → marketing guard misses hard-bounced recipients.
Decide whether spamreport should still trigger admin alert; if yes, call _send_spam_alert inside UNSUBSCRIBE_EVENTS branch too.
Consider upserting users on webhook-driven unsubscribe (parity with /confirm endpoint) so contact-only imports get a marketing_unsubscribed=true user row.
Lower cookie consent banner z-index on /unsubscribe and /desabonnement OR auto-dismiss it there — currently partially covers the CTA.
critical_code_review_comments: routes/unsubscribe.py — clean. Good: _decode handles SignatureExpired vs BadSignature distinctly, SendGrid API failure is caught + logged but DB remains source of truth (correct).

services/email_service.py — suppression guard placed BEFORE _get_sg() so the DB check runs even when SendGrid is mocked/down (verified in tests). Mutating caller's dynamic_data via setdefault is OK but slightly surprising; worth documenting.
UNSUBSCRIBE_SECRET is a separate 64-char secret from JWT_SECRET (good); itsdangerous tokens include timestamp → 30-day TTL enforced at verify time.
Inconsistency: email_suppression (singular) vs email_suppressions (plural) is the biggest risk — two code paths write to different collections. File split recommended once stable.
test_credentials: not needed — unsubscribe flow is tokenised, no login required
seed_data_creation: Created + deleted TEST_unsub_*@example.com users and suppression entries during test runs. Cleanup confirmed.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Webhook signature verification is ON in prod (SENDGRID_WEBHOOK_PUBLIC_KEY set) → live /api/webhooks/sendgrid rejects unsigned test payloads with 403. Tests call _process_events() handler directly instead. To test via HTTP, disable SENDGRID_WEBHOOK_PUBLIC_KEY temporarily or sign the payload with the SDK.
rca of the issue: No unresolved bug. Three minor design inconsistencies identified (listed above).
